title: ABOUTME: the output one per-category audit subagent writes, and the only shape the aggregator will merge
description: A finding is dual-graded: severity says how bad it is if true, verifiability says how firmly code supports it. The two are independent, deliberately. Note what this schema makes impossible rather than merely discouraged: verifiability on a finding admits only PROVEN and PROBABLE, so a MANUAL item cannot be emitted as a finding at all — it belongs in `checklist`. That routing is enforced by construction instead of by instruction.

category.description: The rule category this subagent was dispatched for, mirroring Apple's guideline sections 1-5.

status.description: skipped means the category had no applicable rules for this project, not that it failed.

rule.description: The catalogue rule id this finding came from. Opaque and stable; it does not encode the guideline number, because guideline numbers move.

guideline.description: Apple guideline number as the catalogue records it. Null is a rule with no anchor in Apple's published text — export compliance, for instance, is an App Store Connect requirement rather than a numbered clause.

severity.description: The enum this marketplace already publishes, copied from ios-comprehensive-review rather than imported: plugins here do not depend on each other.

verifiability.description: MANUAL is deliberately absent. An undecidable risk is a checklist item, not a finding.

target.description: The shipping target this finding belongs to. Carried per finding so a rule matched in a widget extension is never reported against the app target.

line.description: Required for PROVEN, optional otherwise. Findings about something ABSENT — no privacy manifest, no account-deletion path — have a file but no line, and forcing one would invent it.

evidence.description: What was actually matched, quoted. Not a restatement of the issue.

unconfirmed.description: Required for PROBABLE: which surrounding context could not be confirmed. A PROBABLE finding that cannot say what is unconfirmed is an unexamined guess.

absence.description: True when the evidence IS the absence of something — no privacy manifest in this target, no account-deletion path anywhere in the source. Such a finding is fully PROVEN and has a file it is about, but no line, because nothing is there to point at. Without this flag the PROVEN-requires-line rule would force a fabricated line number onto the single largest class of App Store rejections, which is the failure the verifiability tier exists to prevent. Required on every finding rather than defaulted, so that whether a finding is about something present or something missing is a stated decision and the line rule cannot be escaped by omission.

resolutions.description: Every change that would resolve this finding. An array because some findings genuinely admit more than one — an unused push entitlement is fixed by deleting the entitlement OR by registering for it, and which is right depends on intent the auditor cannot read. Picking one silently is the bug.

verifiability.description: The only value. A checklist item is by definition the undecidable-from-code case.

item.description: What the developer must check, phrased as an action they can take.

why_manual.description: Why no code scan can decide this — a live URL, a deployed backend, a value that only exists in App Store Connect. Without it a checklist degenerates into everything the auditor could not be bothered to implement.

found_because.description: The scan evidence that made this item apply, for items whose applicability was conditional. Absent means the item always applies.

citation.description: Whether the source this finding leans on was verified during THIS run. Held per source, not per run, so a run that reached Apple's guidelines but not its policy pages is expressible — which is the state a single per-run flag cannot express.

source.description: catalogue means the claim rests on the authored rule alone, which is every citation on a run that reached none of Apple's pages.

appliesTo.description: Present only on a requirement that is regional, dated, or both. Its presence is what routes a finding to the policy sources for verification rather than to the guidelines page.
